page: Amazon Web Services g5.4xlarge belongs to the Accelerated Computing family, configured primarily for GPU-driven workloads such as graphics rendering and machine learning inference. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it is equipped with an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R32 processor providing 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores clocked at 3.3 GHz. The instance includes 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz (4.0 GB per core) and integrates a 10 Gbps baseline network capability. Local high-speed storage is bundled via a 600 GB NVMe SSD.

Hardware acceleration is supplied by a single NVIDIA A10G GPU built on the Ampere architecture, providing 22 GB of dedicated VRAM. The system features AVX instruction support along with hardware AES and SHA cryptographic instructions, though it lacks AVX-512 extensions and AMX accelerator tiles. The presence of the dedicated A10G GPU makes it distinct from general-purpose virtual machines by offloading parallel floating-point processing directly to hardware.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution in GPU-centric machine learning tasks. LLM inference metrics register in the top 10%, reaching 9391.67 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 429.59 tokens/sec for text generation with small 135M models. For medium 7B models, it achieves 2891.56 tokens/sec prompt processing and 94.48 tokens/sec text generation. Prompt processing on large 70B models delivers 36.15 tokens/sec. Conversely, CPU metrics are moderate: Geekbench scores are 1340.0 single-core and 8024.0 multi-core, while PassMark reports a CPU score of 19544.7 and a memory score of 2667.93. Uncached memory read and write bandwidths measure at 37.02 GB/sec and 22.53 GB/sec, respectively.

The primary tradeoff of the g5.4xlarge centers on its focus on GPU throughput versus host CPU and uncached memory speed. The configuration provides strong cost efficiency for GPU acceleration by bundling local NVMe storage and dedicated Ampere hardware without requiring a full multi-GPU instance. This makes it an appropriate fit for LLM inference, real-time graphics rendering, video processing, and GPU-accelerated machine learning workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services g5.4xlarge is an accelerated computing instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It integrates an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R32 processor featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores) running at 3.3 GHz, 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and a 10 Gbps baseline network speed. The instance is bundled with a 600 GB NVMe SSD for fast local storage and a dedicated NVIDIA A10G Ampere GPU equipped with 22 GB of VRAM. Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance for LLM inference workloads, delivering 94.48 tokens/sec text generation on 7B parameter models, while general CPU and memory bandwidth benchmarks perform in the middle range. The hardware configuration makes this server optimal for graphics rendering, media encoding, and machine learning inference tasks.
